title: Continuity of Ext out of a constructible complex
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the condensed coefficient rings $\underline E$, $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$, or $\underline{\mathcal O}_E$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and work in the ordinary derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ of module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For a locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$, write $a=i\circ u$ with $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ closed and $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open, and put $a_!L=i_*u_!L$, with the module-object pushforward of [def-sfb-module-lower-star] and open extension by zero of [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. A finite locally free (or lisse) $\Lambda_S$-module means one that is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of $\Lambda_S$ locally for the pro-étale topology.

Let $C$ be obtained by finitely many extensions, shifts and isomorphisms from such $a_!L$. Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of complexes of $\Lambda_X$-modules with a common integer $b$ such that $K_i^r=0$ for every $i$ and $r<b$. Put $K^\bullet=\varinjlim_iK_i^\bullet$, the termwise colimit in module objects. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map induced by $K_i^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups:
$$
\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})}(C,K_i^\bullet[q])
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})}(C,K^\bullet[q]).
$$
The hypothesis on $C$ holds for every bounded constructible complex when $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$, with constructibility and the bounded constructible category as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. In particular, for every constructible sheaf $C$ with either of these coefficients, all $\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\Lambda_X}(C,-)$ commute with filtered colimits of module objects, where $\operatorname{Ext}^q(C,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})}(C,M[q])$ for sheaves regarded as degree-zero complexes. For $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O}_E$, the hypothesis holds for every finite iterated extension of sheaves $a_!L_0$ with $L_0$ finite locally free over $\Lambda_S$.

proof.text:
For the fixed filtered diagram let $\mathcal C$ consist of the objects $D$ whose comparison $\alpha_D^q$ is bijective for every $q$. For a distinguished triangle $D'\to D\to D''\to D'[1]$, [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact], applied to its rotations, gives the natural exact five-term segment
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(D',K_i[q-1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(D'',K_i[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}(D,K_i[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}(D',K_i[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}(D'',K_i[q+1]).
$$
Taking the filtered colimit leaves this segment exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. Compare it with the segment for $K$: if $D',D''\in\mathcal C$, all four outer vertical maps are isomorphisms, so [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] makes $\alpha_D^q$ an isomorphism. For shifts, the natural identities $\operatorname{Hom}(D[n],K_i[q])=\operatorname{Hom}(D,K_i[q - n])$ identify the comparison for $D[n]$ with that for $D$ in degree $q-n$. Precomposition with an isomorphism $D\simeq D_0$ identifies the two comparison maps. Also $0\in\mathcal C$, since both groups vanish. Thus $\mathcal C$ is closed under extensions, shifts and isomorphisms; rotating the cone triangle $A\to B\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)\to A[1]$ shows that it is closed under cones of morphisms between its objects.

proof.text: For a generator $a_!L$, $X$ is quasi-compact by the Noetherian definition and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Every open $W\subseteq X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The image of the immersion $a$ over any affine open of $X$ is locally closed, hence closed in an open subset of $X$; that open subset is compact, so the image is compact. Since an immersion is a homeomorphism onto its image, $a$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-pqf-qc-immersion-open-closed-factor] to choose $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $i$ closed and $u$ open. Thus the open complement $V=X\setminus Z$ is quasi-compact and its immersion $j$ is quasi-compact: the inverse image of any affine open of $X$ is again an open of $X$. Every open of $Z$ is $Z\cap W$ for an open $W\subseteq X$ and is closed in that compact $W$, hence quasi-compact. In particular the inverse image under $u$ of each affine open of $Z$ is quasi-compact, so $u$ is quasi-compact. Our three coefficient rings are among the admissible rings in [det-lem-constructible-ext-continuity-stratum]; $L$ is finite locally free and the diagram has the same common lower bound $b$. That node therefore gives exactly the canonical comparison isomorphism for $a_!L$ in every degree.

Inducting on the finite expression of $C$ now proves the displayed comparison: the generator case is step 2, and each shift, isomorphism, or extension is handled by step 1. This induction is finite by the hypothesis on $C$.

When $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$, [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation] applies with precisely our Noetherian hypothesis on $X$: every bounded constructible $C$ is obtained by finitely many cones from $a_!L[n]$, where lisse means the finite locally free condition in our statement. The generator comparison is step 2; the shift, cone and isomorphism closure in step 1, followed by induction on that finite sequence, gives the comparison for $C$. The same finite sequence expresses $C$ by extensions and shifts, since a cone triangle rotates to $B\to\operatorname{Cone}(A\to B)\to A[1]\to B[1]$. For a constructible sheaf in degree zero, [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] places it in the bounded constructible category. A diagram of sheaves in degree zero has common lower bound $b=0$ and its termwise colimit is the sheaf colimit in degree zero; by the definition of $\operatorname{Ext}^q$ in the statement the comparison is exactly the asserted Ext colimit isomorphism.

For $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O}_E$, choose the given finite extension filtration $0=C_0\subset\cdots\subset C_m=C$, with $C_k/C_{k-1}=a_{k!}L_{0,k}$. The base $C_0=0$ belongs to $\mathcal C$ by step 1, each quotient belongs by step 2, and [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] turns each short exact sequence into a triangle $C_{k-1}\to C_k\to a_{k!}L_{0,k}\to C_{k-1}[1]$ in the derived category. The extension argument of step 1, inductively for $k=1,\ldots,m$, gives the integral clause.
